reasons: Classification is correct: Section 13 already gives 12-month auto-renewals with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice (preferred on term and window), but there is no pre-renewal reminder and renewal pricing is uncapped beyond the first-year freeze in Section 6, so the clause falls short of both the preferred and the fallback pricing position — a genuine deviation.

Redline is targeted and directionally right: it inserts a 60-day TrueLink renewal/fee-change notice into p0078 without disturbing the existing 30-day opt-out, and adds a renewal uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%) into the existing fee-freeze sentence in p0047, leaving the favorable most-favored-rate language intact.

The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' check is a regex artifact — the operative 'thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year' language is retained and already complies; the 0.659 changed-character ratio on p0047 reflects the necessary addition of a cap to a short sentence, not an over-broad rewrite.
Comment is accurate, concise, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the 5% fallback.

Minor drafting nit (not disqualifying): the cap mixes units — '(i) the increase in the Consumer Price Index' (a percentage) against '(ii) three percent (3%) of the fees in effect for the immediately preceding term' (an amount); consider phrasing both as percentage increases over the prior term's fees, and add a comma before the final 'and that rates charged...' for readability.
